concept.name: Cup and handle
concept.definition: A bullish continuation pattern popularized by William O'Neil in 'How to Make Money in Stocks' (1988), consisting of a U-shaped consolidation (the cup) followed by a smaller downward-drifting pullback (the handle) on the right side, completed by a breakout above the handle's resistance. The cup resembles a rounding bottom within an existing uptrend. It is a technical-analysis hypothesis, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: After a strong rally the stock digests its gains in a wide bowl; the small final dip (the handle) shakes out the last weak holders before the uptrend resumes through the old high.
concept.mechanics: Require a prior uptrend a few months old; the cup should be U-shaped (a sharp V is disqualifying) and ideally retrace no more than one-third to one-half of the prior advance. The handle forms in the upper half of the cup, retracing up to roughly one-third of the cup's advance, over one to several weeks. The trigger is a breakout above handle resistance with a substantial volume increase; the target projects the cup's depth from the breakout point.
concept.formula: Price target = B + (R - C), where B = breakout price above handle resistance, R = right peak of the cup, and C = low of the cup.
concept.failure_modes: Handles that drift too deep (retracing more than half the cup) or form in the cup's lower half signal weak demand and high failure rates; low-volume breakouts frequently fail. In bear markets the breakout often becomes a bull trap at the old high.
concept.misconceptions: That any V-shaped dip followed by a pullback qualifies — O'Neil's specification demands a rounded U cup, a shallow handle in the upper half, and volume expansion on the breakout. Also that the pattern works without a prior uptrend; it is a continuation pattern by construction.
concept.example: A stock runs from $10 to $32.69, rounds out a three-month cup with a 42% retracement, forms a six-week handle, then gaps above handle resistance at $32 on surging volume; the measured target is about $41.
